doc.title: Jerry Bergonzi interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 7, 2022

title: Suggesting what to practice: jazz yoga
summary: He suggests rather than tells students what to practice and says he practices for the zone, which he calls jazz yoga.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: So now you tell your students what to practice. People weren’t telling you but you tell them. Is that too simplistic?

No but a few words in there that I would change and I suggest what to practice. I don’t tell anybody anything. I mean — you know what I mean? I say if you do this, this is really going to help. But I always leave the decision whether they want to practice or not. I tell them I don’t really care if you practice. I don’t care if you get better. And as a matter of fact I practice ‘cause I don’t care if I get better. I practice because I like practicing. It puts me in a space, a zone. I call it jazz yoga. I get in that zone physically,
emotionally, spiritually, mentally. If you don’t want to practice cool. You know I mean what can I tell you?
And they’re paying a hefty sum to be there.
And so there’s some motivation there.
